name: Mary Cassatt

notes.name: Wikipedia · Mary Cassatt
notes.q: In 1868, one of her paintings, A Mandoline Player, was accepted for the first time by the selection jury for the Paris Salon.

src.name: Wikipedia · Mary Cassatt
src.q: After overcoming her father's objections, she moved to Paris in 1866, with her mother and family friends acting as chaperones.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Mary Cassatt
notes.q: Her painting Two Women Throwing Flowers During Carnival was well received in the Salon of 1872 and was purchased.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Mary Cassatt
notes.q: She wrote in a letter of July 1871, "I have given up my studio & torn up my father's portrait, & have not touched a brush for six weeks nor ever will again until I see some prospect of getting back to Europe.

src.name: Wikipedia · Mary Cassatt
src.q: Cassatt traveled to Chicago to try her luck, but lost some of her early paintings in the Great Chicago Fire of 1871.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Mary Cassatt
notes.q: At this low point in her career, she was invited by Edgar Degas to show her works with the Impressionists, a group that had begun their own series of independent exhibitions in 1874 with much attendant notoriety.

src.name: Wikipedia · Mary Cassatt
src.q: After completing her commission for the bishop, Cassatt traveled to Madrid and Seville, where she painted a group of paintings of Spanish subjects, including Spanish Dancer Wearing a Lace Mantilla (1873, in the National Museum of American Art, Smithsonian Institution).
